data.turoyo: Əmmi azze, kḥoyər, kit pire, kətla gulloke mi xaṣrayo ḥḏo mayo. Omər məlle: “Ḥulto, mə ksaymat?” Əmmo: “Ono, kurem, i šawayto du yawmo w du lalyo no.”
data.translation: Als er so ging, sah er eine alte Frau, die hatte einen Knäuel rechts und einen Knäuel links. - Tante, was machst du denn da? - Mein Junge, ich bin die Aufwicklerin des Tages und der Nacht. -

rationale: Thin Part act. I.1, adding the feminine šawayto alongside existing masculine šawoyo.

summary: Preterit šwele, Infectum kšowenole/gšoweno/šowat, Imperativ šway and masculine/feminine Part act. šawoyo/šawayto form a coherent winding paradigm. No extra stem or Detransitive form is evidenced.
Time objects are explicit or recoverable and may be resumed by -le. Agent identity is expressed by the Part act. with copula, while the finite winding events have an agent and yarn/time theme.
Three reader additions duplicate the entry's exact 69/358,361,362 quotations; additions are restricted to new participant/form contexts in the thin cells.
Confirm whether the listed etymology from MEA šby 'take captive' is appropriate for this winding homonym. The supplied evidence establishes winding but does not resolve its historical derivation.
Does šawayto function productively as the feminine Part act. in ordinary speech, or primarily as the narrative agent designation here? Existing category is retained.

rationale: The German past tense of wickeln is “wickelte”, also the reading of the supplied edition.
“Halbe” modifies the following noun “Stunde” and is not substantivized; the edition has “eine halbe Stunde”.
“Halbe” is an attributive adjective before “Stunde”, so it is lowercase; the edition likewise prints “eine halbe Stunde”.

summary: Day and night are represented as tangible yarn being wound in fantastic narrative; this participant extension is already presupposed by the existing Part act. example, not a separate temporal sense.
